concepts.title: Choosing Graphs and Diagrams
concepts.definition: Graphic representation turns processed data into line graphs for trends, bar diagrams for comparison, pie diagrams for shares and pictograms for popular communication; the choice depends on the nature of data and the message intended.
concepts.key_idea: Each diagram answers a different question: lines ask how it changed, bars ask how they compare, pies ask how it divides.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy303.txt types of diagrams and their choice sections

solution_steps.explain: line graphs, bar diagrams, pie diagrams and pictograms are the core set
time series take lines, component shares take pies
the message chooses the medium, not fashion

concepts.title: Constructing a Pie Diagram
concepts.definition: A pie diagram divides a circle of 360 degrees among component shares; the angle for each component equals its share of the total multiplied by 360 divided by 100 when shares are percentages, and the sectors are then arranged and shaded distinctly.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying each percentage share by 3.6 gives its sector angle in degrees.

solution_steps.explain: shares are given as percentages summing to 100

concepts.title: Line Graphs and Bar Diagrams
concepts.definition: Line graphs plot values against a continuous axis, ideal for temperature and rainfall trends over months or years; bar diagrams raise rectangles of equal width whose lengths are proportional to values, simple bars for one series, multiple bars for comparison and compound bars for totals with components.
concepts.key_idea: The y-axis scale decides honesty: too large a scale exaggerates change, too small hides it.

concepts.title: Thematic Maps as Data Presentation
concepts.definition: Maps present spatial data through dot maps for distribution, choropleth maps for density ratios by units, and isopleth maps joining equal values like contour lines; the choice follows whether data are points, ratios or continuous surfaces.
concepts.key_idea: Geography's signature diagram is the map: dots count, shades compare and isolines connect.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy303.txt dot, choropleth and isopleth map sections

solution_steps.explain: dots for totals, choropleth for ratios, isopleths for surfaces
population totals take dots, density takes choropleth shading
each map type carries its own legend discipline
